provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Letter Oo
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the sound of O.
The pupils should be able to trace capital O and small o.
Introduction:
We have learned many letters. Today we learn letter Oo.
Oo is in orange we eat for vitamin.
Content:
O says /o/ as in orange. Show orange fruit.
Capital O is round like a wheel. Trace O in air.
Small o is also round but smaller. Trace o in sand.
Class activity:
Children make big O with their bodies on the floor.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does O make?
Show me how to write capital O.
Trace small o on the board.
Summary:
Today we learned letter Oo and its sound.

topics.title: Letter Pp
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of P.
The pupils should be able to trace capital P and small p.
Introduction:
Last week we learned letter Oo. Today we learn Pp.
Pp is in pen we write with.
Content:
P says /p/ as in pen. Show a pen.
Capital P has a straight line and a round part. Trace P with chalk.
Small p has a straight line and a round part below. Trace p with finger.
Class activity:
Children pretend to pop balloons when they hear P sound.
Evaluation questions:
What word starts with P sound?
Draw capital P in the air.
Trace small p on your slate.
Summary:
We learned letter Pp today. P says /p/.

topics.title: Letter Qq
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to produce the sound of Q.
The pupils should be able to trace capital Q and small q.
Introduction:
We learned Oo and Pp. Now we learn Qq.
Qq is in queen like our teacher.
Content:
Q says /k/ as in queen. Show queen picture.
Capital Q is O with a tail. Trace Q with big movement.
Small q is o with a tail. Trace q with small movement.
Class activity:
Children march and say /k/ /k/ queen when they see Q card.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does Q make?
Show how to write capital Q.
Trace small q on the sand.
Summary:
Today we learned letter Qq. Q is for queen.

topics.title: Letter Rr
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the sound of R.
The pupils should be able to trace capital R and small r.
Introduction:
We learned Qq last week. Today we learn Rr.
Rr is in rope we play with.
Content:
R says /r/ as in rope. Show a rope.
Capital R has a straight line and a curve. Trace R with arm movement.
Small r has a curve and a leg down. Trace r with finger.
Class activity:
Children make rope sound /r/ /r/ while moving arms like rope.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does R make?
Draw capital R in your notebook.
Trace small r on the board.
Summary:
We learned letter Rr today. R says /r/.

topics.title: Letter Ss
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sound of S.
The pupils should be able to trace capital S and small s.
Introduction:
Last week we learned Rr. Now we learn Ss.
Ss is in sun we see every day.
Content:
S says /s/ as in sun. Show sun picture.
Capital S is like a snake curve. Trace S with whole arm.
Small s is also a snake curve but smaller. Trace s with finger.
Class activity:
Children hiss like snakes when they see S card.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does S make?
Show me how to write capital S.
Trace small s on your slate.
Summary:
Today we learned letter Ss. S says /s/.

topics.title: Letter Tt
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to produce the sound of T.
The pupils should be able to trace capital T and small t.
Introduction:
We learned Ss last week. Today we learn Tt.
Tt is in tap we get water from.
Content:
T says /t/ as in tap. Show a tap.
Capital T has a straight line across and down. Trace T with ruler.
Small t has a straight line down and curve. Trace t with stick.
Class activity:
Children pretend to turn on tap when they hear T sound.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does T make?
Draw capital T on the board.
Trace small t in your book.
Summary:
We learned letter Tt today. T says /t/.

topics.title: Letter Uu
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the sound of U.
The pupils should be able to trace capital U and small u.
Introduction:
Last week we learned Tt. Now we learn Uu.
Uu is in umbrella we use when rain falls.
Content:
U says /u/ as in umbrella. Show an umbrella.
Capital U is like a cup shape. Trace U with both hands.
Small u is also a cup shape but smaller. Trace u with one finger.
Class activity:
Children open and close hands like umbrella when they see U.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does U make?
Show how to write capital U.
Trace small u on the sand.
Summary:
Today we learned letter Uu. U is for umbrella.

topics.title: Letter Vv and Ww
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the sounds of V and W.
The pupils should be able to trace Vv and Ww.
Introduction:
We learned Uu last week. Today we learn Vv and Ww.
Vv is in van we ride in.
Ww is in water we drink.
Content:
V says /v/ as in van. Show van picture.
W says /w/ as in water. Show water bottle.
Capital V has two slants meeting at bottom. Trace V with chalk.
Capital W has two V shapes together. Trace W with arm.
Class activity:
Children drive van for V and swim for W when letters shown.
Evaluation questions:
What sound does V make?
What sound does W make?
Trace capital V and W on your slate.
Summary:
We learned Vv and Ww today. V says /v/ and W says /w/.

topics.title: Letters Oo to Ww
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say sounds from O to W.
The pupils should be able to circle the letter the teacher says.
The pupils should be able to trace letters neatly.
Introduction:
We have learned many letters. Let's recall Oo to Ww.
We will play a game and trace letters.
Content:
Say sounds from Oo to Ww together. Point to each letter chart.
Teacher says a sound, pupils circle the right letter on paper.
Trace each letter from O to W with pencil in notebook.
Class activity:
Children stand when hear their letter sound from O to W.
Evaluation questions:
Say all sounds from O to W.
Circle the letter that says /o/.
Trace capital R and small s neatly.
Summary:
Today we practiced letters Oo to Ww. We know their sounds.

topics.title: Revision of all letters
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say the whole alphabet.
The pupils should be able to match letters to pictures.
The pupils should be able to trace letters freely.
Introduction:
We learned many letters this term. Let's revise all.
We will say alphabet and play matching game.
Content:
Say the whole alphabet together from A to Z. Point to alphabet chart.
Match each letter to its picture. A for apple, B for ball etc.
Trace any letter you like on paper. Use different colors.
Class activity:
Children march in circle saying alphabet when music plays.
Evaluation questions:
Say the whole alphabet.\Match A to apple picture.\Which letter comes after P?
Trace your favorite letter.
Summary:
We revised all letters today. We know alphabet from A to Z.
